subject: Console telemetry: first-party tagging, consent flow and DPA implications
messages:
From: privacy@brightlayer.com
To: jonas.weber@redwood.com
Cc: 
Date: Tue, 3 Nov 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Quick questions on Console telemetry & marketing analytics (BrightLayer)

Hi Jonas,

Thanks again for the product demo yesterday — the Console looks promising. Before we proceed to legal review we'd like to clarify how Console telemetry and the marketing analytics integrations interact with our site tagging. A few specific asks from our privacy and security team: 

- What telemetry is sent back to Redwood by default from the Console (events, URLs, IPs, user-agent, account IDs)?
- Do you use first-party tagging (server-side or client-side) or rely on third-party cookies for marketing analytics?
- Can telemetry be configured so product operational metrics are separate from marketing/analytics signals?
- What subprocessors handle telemetry storage/processing, and where are they located?
- For EU-resident data, what transfers/controls do you rely on (SCCs, adequacy, etc.)?
- Retention policy for telemetry and the ability for BrightLayer to request deletion/export.

I've attached our short privacy questionnaire. Could you send your DPA and a dataflow diagram (high level) to help our GC and privacy team evaluate?

Happy to set up a quick call if easier — copying Elena Moreno, our external privacy advisor, on this thread.

Best,
Marta Ruiz
Privacy & Compliance Lead
BrightLayer
privacy@brightlayer.com

[Attachment: BrightLayer_Privacy_Questionnaire.xlsx]

From: jonas.weber@redwood.com
To: privacy@brightlayer.com
Cc: grace.oconnor@redwood.com, lauren.bishop@redwood.com
Date: Tue, 3 Nov 2026 11:06:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Quick questions on Console telemetry & marketing analytics (BrightLayer)

Hi Marta — thanks for the clear list. High-level answers below and I attached our DPA + a simple telemetry diagram. Grace (Privacy Program) and Lauren (Account Director) are looped in to handle the details and schedule a follow-up.

- Default telemetry: product usage events, anonymized client metrics (latency, errors), account identifier (account id), IPs are captured for fraud/abuse and may be pseudonymized in analytics exports. We do not collect raw PII by default unless instrumented by the customer.
- Tagging model: Redwood supports first-party tagging (we recommend server-side tagging for marketing integrations). We also support client-side SDKs but marketing pixels that require third-party cookies are customer-configured — Redwood itself does not inject third-party cookies by default.
- Separation of signals: yes — Console can be configured with separate pipelines: product telemetry (operational) and marketing analytics (marketing tags). We advise separate streams and different retention settings.
- Subprocessors: see DPA appendix A in attached PDF; primary processors include CloudInfraCo (EU & us regions), LogStorePro (metrics indexing), and AnalyticsEdge (optional marketing integrations). Locations listed in appendix.
- Transfers & controls: we rely on SCCs for EU->US transfers and can provide executed SCCs or a registry of executed agreements.
- Retention: default 90 days for detailed telemetry, aggregated metrics retained for 24 months; export/delete on request (we provide automated export tool for account admins).

Next steps: Lauren can coordinate a technical session to walk through telemetry tagging options and Grace can coordinate the DPA/subprocessor review. Are you available Thursday afternoon for a 60-min sync?

Thanks — attaching: Redwood_DPA_v2.pdf, Telemetry-data-flow.png

Best,
Jonas Weber
Senior Account Executive
Redwood Inference
jonas.weber@redwood.com
[Attachments: Redwood_DPA_v2.pdf, Telemetry-data-flow.png]

From: elena@privacyconsults.io
To: jonas.weber@redwood.com, privacy@brightlayer.com
Cc: grace.oconnor@redwood.com
Date: Wed, 4 Nov 2026 08:43:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Quick questions on Console telemetry & marketing analytics (BrightLayer)

Thanks Jonas — a few follow-ups from BrightLayer's privacy review after an initial read of the DPA and diagram: 

- Subprocessor detail: Appendix A lists vendors but no specific subprocessed data fields per vendor. Can you confirm which vendor sees raw IPs, which sees pseudonymized identifiers only, and who has access to account IDs?
- Pseudonymization: is IP truncation applied before it reaches LogStorePro/AnalyticsEdge? Is there a toggle at the account level?
- Marketing analytics: you mention "optional marketing integrations" — does Redwood act as a controller or processor for marketing tag execution? BrightLayer wants to ensure "pure first-party server-side" tagging so that marketing providers cannot correlate BrightLayer users with other customers.
- SCCs: can Redwood provide a template of the SCCs you execute? We also need the timeline for execution (BrightLayer legal typically requires SCCs signed or an interim DPA with SCC annexes).
- Data subject rights: confirm the process and SLA for deletion requests originating from an EU end-user (RTA for deletion and for targeted marketing signals).
- Audit evidence: can Redwood provide logs showing subprocessors' access for the prior 90 days if requested?

A few practical asks: if you can produce a mapping CSV that ties fields -> processor -> storage location and a short note on whether retention is configurable per account, that would help speed legal review.

On the technical side, we also want clarity on whether the Console pushes marketing events to third-party endpoints directly from the customer's browser (client-side) or whether they pass through Redwood servers where you can enforce filtering/PII removal.

Appreciate the quick turnaround — happy to take the technical call after you provide the mapping.

Best regards,
Elena Moreno
Principal Consultant, PrivacyConsults
elena@privacyconsults.io

From: jonas.weber@redwood.com
To: privacy@brightlayer.com
Cc: grace.oconnor@redwood.com, lauren.bishop@redwood.com
Date: Thu, 5 Nov 2026 16:20:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Quick questions on Console telemetry & marketing analytics (BrightLayer)

Hi Marta / Elena — thanks for the detailed follow-ups. Grace and I worked through the questions and below is a concise mapping + next steps. I've also uploaded a short SCC execution plan.

Mapping summary (brief):
- CloudInfraCo (primary compute/storage): receives product telemetry (events, account id, truncated IP). IP truncation applied at ingress; raw IPs are only available to our security team under strict access controls.
- LogStorePro (indexing/metrics): receives pseudonymized IDs and aggregated metrics; IPs are never sent raw.
- AnalyticsEdge (marketing integrations): optional and only used if customer opts into marketing connectors; when enabled, the Console can act as a server-side forwarder (Redwood as processor) which lets BrightLayer keep control — Redwood will not co-mingle identifiers across customers. If customers choose client-side third-party pixels, those requests go directly from the end-user browser to the vendor and are outside of Redwood's processing scope.

Retention/config: retention windows are configurable per account; default is 90 days for detailed events, 24 months for aggregates. Deletion requests: account admins can trigger exports/deletes via the Console API; for DSRs we commit to 30-day SLA after verification.

SCCs & DPA: attached is our recommended SCC execution checklist and we can provide executed SCCs within 10 business days once templates are agreed.

Audit logs: we can produce subprocessors access logs for a rolling 90-day window — this requires a signed Data Access Request (standard for enterprise).

Action items:
- Lauren: propose two time slots for a joint technical + legal sync (I've blocked Fri 11/6 10:00-11:00 PT and Mon 11/9 08:00-09:00 PT tentatively)
- Grace: prepping a CSV mapping fields->processor->location (will upload by EOD Friday)
- BrightLayer: confirm whether you prefer server-side forwarding for marketing connectors or will rely on client-side pixels (this affects processor scope).

If acceptable, we can put the DPA in DocuSign and start SCC acceptance flows.

Best,
Jonas Weber
Senior Account Executive
Redwood Inference
jonas.weber@redwood.com
